shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Starting from an even 1A, 1B, 1C bundle, trading 1A for 1B would make my inventory less balanced (0A, 2B, 1C). Since I value variety, this lowers my utility.
Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading 1 B for 1 A would create imbalance (2A/0B/1C). Since I value the goods equally and prefer variety, this reduces my utility.
Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes my inventory to A:3, B:0, C:1. I gain more total goods, and the increase outweighs the loss despite reduced variety.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C. Trading 1 C for 1 B would make my bundle less balanced (A:1, B:2, C:0), which reduces utility given my preference for variety.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, trading 1×B for 1×C would make my inventory less balanced (2×C, 0×B, 1×A). Since I value variety and currently have equal amounts, this lowers my utility.

Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (3,0,1). I receive more total goods, and C becomes abundant while B becomes scarce; since I value all goods equally and value scarcer goods more, the gain of two units outweighs giving one unit.
I value A, B, and C equally, and this trade would change my balanced inventory from 1A/1B/1C to 0A/2B/1C, reducing variety and lowering my utility.
With 1 of each good, my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1 B for 1 A would make my inventory less varied (A:2, B:0, C:1), which lowers utility for my preference for variety.

Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes my inventory from (A1,B1,C1) to (A3,B0,C1). I value variety, so this reduces balance, but the gain of two units outweighs the loss of one and increases my overall bundle value.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C, so swapping 1 C for 1 B would reduce variety and make my bundle less balanced.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, exchanging 1 B for 1 C would make my inventory less balanced (C:2, B:0, A:1), which reduces utility given my preference for variety.

Starting from an even bundle of 1A, 1B, 1C, trading 1B for 2C gives me 1A, 0B, 3C. Since I value goods equally and prefer variety, losing my only B and becoming less balanced reduces my utility despite receiving more total units.
With inventory A:1, B:1, C:1, swapping 1 A for 1 B would make my bundle less balanced (A:0, B:2, C:1). Since I value variety and currently hold all goods equally, this trade lowers my utility.
Starting from 1A, 1B, 1C, all goods are equally represented. Trading 1B for 1A changes my bundle to 2A, 0B, 1C, which reduces variety and lowers utility under my preference for balanced holdings.

Starting from an even bundle (1A, 1B, 1C), giving 1 B and receiving 2 A results in 3A, 0B, 1C. Since I value variety and goods I have less of more highly, losing my only B and creating a more imbalanced bundle reduces my utility despite the extra quantity.
Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading 1C for 1B would make my inventory less balanced (1A/2B/0C). Since I value variety and currently value all goods equally, this reduces my utility.

Starting from an even bundle of A, B, and C, swapping 1 B for 1 C changes my inventory to A:1, B:0, C:2. Since I value goods equally but prefer variety and relatively value scarcer goods more, this trade makes my bundle less balanced and does not increase my utility.
Trading 1 B for 2 C increases my total goods and gives a net gain. Although it reduces variety slightly, the extra unit overall makes this bundle better for me.
I currently have no B and one A, so swapping 1 A for 1 B increases variety and improves my balance across goods.
I currently have no B and a surplus of C, so exchanging 1 C for 1 B increases variety and improves my bundle.

I currently have no B and several C, so gaining 1 B increases variety and balances my inventory. Giving 2 C still leaves me with some C, and this trade improves my bundle based on my preference for goods I have less of.
With inventory A:1, B:1, C:1, my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1 A for 1 B would make it less varied (A:0, B:2, C:1), which lowers my utility.
I currently have one of each good, so my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×B for 1×A would create an imbalance without increasing total value, so it does not improve my utility.

Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes my inventory from (1 C, 1 B, 1 A) to (1 C, 0 B, 3 A). Receiving two goods for one increases my total holdings, and the gain in A outweighs the loss of B for my utility.
Trading 1×C for 1×B changes my balanced inventory from {A:1, B:1, C:1} to {A:1, B:2, C:0}, which reduces variety and lowers my utility.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C, so swapping 1 B for 1 C would reduce variety and make my bundle less balanced.

Starting from a balanced bundle (1 A, 1 B, 1 C), giving 1 B and receiving 2 C yields (1 A, 0 B, 3 C). Since I value variety, losing B entirely and becoming more imbalanced reduces my utility despite gaining total quantity.

Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from (A:2, B:1, C:0) to (A:1, B:2, C:0). Since A and B are equally valued and I currently have more A than B, giving up one of the more abundant good for one of the less abundant good improves variety without reducing total goods.

I currently have fewer C and B than A, so B is more valuable than A, but after this trade my inventory becomes A:3, B:0, C:0, which is less balanced than before. Giving away my only B for an extra A reduces variety and lowers my utility.

I currently have no C, so variety makes C most valuable, then A and B are roughly similar. Trading 2 A for 1 B would leave me with a less balanced bundle (0 C, 2 B, 0 A) than my current inventory (0 C, 1 B, 2 A), so it does not improve my utility.

Accepting improves variety: I give up 1 B from a bundle with no C and more A, and receive 2 A. Since I currently have no C, B is more valuable than A, but getting 2 A for 1 B is still a favorable increase in total goods and utility.
Trading 1 B for 1 C improves variety: I currently have no C and only 1 B, so gaining the missing good increases my utility more than keeping the extra B.
Giving 1 B and receiving 2 C improves variety: I currently have no C, so C is especially valuable, while parting with my only B is outweighed by gaining two units of the good I lack most.
Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading 1 A for 1 B would create 0A/2B/1C, reducing variety and therefore lowering my utility.

Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading 1 B for 1 A would make my inventory less balanced (2A/0B/1C). Since I value variety and currently all goods are equally represented, this trade lowers my utility.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A leaves me with 1 C, 0 B, 3 A. Since I prefer variety and this makes my holdings much less balanced, it does not increase my utility.
With inventory C=1, B=1, A=1, I currently have perfect variety. Trading 1×C for 1×B would make my bundle less balanced (C=0, B=2, A=1), so it lowers my utility.
With 1 each of A, B, and C, my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1 B for 1 C would make it less varied (A:1, B:0, C:2), so it lowers my utility.

Starting from an even bundle (1 A, 1 B, 1 C), trading 1 B for 2 C gives me more total goods and remains fairly balanced overall. The gain of two units outweighs the loss of one equal-valued unit, so this increases my utility.

Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from A:2, B:1, C:0 to A:1, B:2, C:0. Since I value goods equally but prefer variety, reducing my surplus of A in exchange for B does not lower utility and keeps my bundle balanced enough to justify the trade.
I currently have fewer B than A, so B is more valuable to me for variety. Trading 1 B for 1 A would make my inventory less balanced, not more useful.
This trade reduces variety and leaves me with only B. Giving 2 A for 1 B does not improve my bundle given I already have B and have no C.
Accepting improves variety: I give up 1 B from a balanced need, and gain 2 A, increasing my total goods without giving away my scarcest good C.
Trading 1 B for 1 C increases my variety by replacing a duplicate with a good I currently lack, improving my bundle.
C is my scarcest good and I currently have none, while I have 1 B. Receiving 2 C for 1 B increases variety and improves my bundle.
With inventory A=1, B=1, C=1, I currently have perfect variety. Trading 1 A for 1 B would make my bundle less balanced (A=0, B=2, C=1), which lowers utility under my variety preference.

Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading 1 B for 1 A gives me 2A/0B/1C, which reduces variety. Since I value all goods equally and prefer having more of what I currently have less of, this trade lowers my utility.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A results in 1 C, 0 B, 3 A. The gain of two goods outweighs the loss of one, so this increases my utility despite reducing variety.
With inventory C:1, B:1, A:1, I currently have perfect variety. Trading 1×C for 1×B would make my bundle less balanced (C:0, B:2, A:1), so it lowers my utility.
I currently have one of each good, which is already perfectly balanced for my variety preference. Trading 1 B for 1 C would make my inventory less balanced (C:2, B:0, A:1), so it reduces my utility.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory to 3 C, 0 B, 1 A. Since I value variety and this makes my bundle much less balanced, it reduces my utility.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves variety in my inventory, changing it from A:2, B:0, C:1 to A:1, B:1, C:1, which better matches my equal-value, variety-seeking preferences.
Trading 2 A for 1 B changes my inventory from (C1, B0, A2) to (C1, B1, A0), which is more balanced and improves variety, so it increases my utility.
Trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety: I currently have no B and only 1 C, so gaining the missing good is more valuable than keeping an extra C-equivalent.
